definition: An AWS service that provisions and manages AWS infrastructure using template files written in JSON or YAML, enabling Infrastructure as Code.
A collection of AWS resources that CloudFormation creates, updates, and deletes together as a single unit based on a template.
A JSON or YAML text file that describes the AWS resources (and their configurations) you want CloudFormation to create. It is the blueprint, not the infrastructure itself.
The practice of managing and provisioning computing infrastructure through machine-readable text files, rather than through manual interactive configuration tools.
Optional template section that defines input variables, allowing you to customize a template at deployment time without modifying the template file.
The only mandatory section in a CloudFormation template. It declares all the AWS resources to be created, such as EC2 instances, VPCs, and security groups.
Optional template section that declares values to display after stack creation. Outputs can be exported for use by other stacks via cross-stack references.
An intrinsic function that imports a value exported by another CloudFormation stack's Outputs section, enabling cross-stack references.
A mechanism where one CloudFormation stack imports output values exported by another stack, allowing stacks to share resources like VPC IDs and Subnet IDs.
An attribute on a CloudFormation resource that controls what happens to the resource when its stack is deleted. Options: Delete (default), Retain, Snapshot.
A preview of the changes CloudFormation will make to a stack when an update is applied, showing which resources will be added, modified, or deleted before any action is taken.
A CloudFormation intrinsic function that returns the value of a parameter or the physical ID of a resource.
A CloudFormation intrinsic function for string substitution. Replaces variable placeholders like ${AWS::StackName} with their actual values at runtime.
A CloudFormation intrinsic function that retrieves a specific attribute of a resource. Example: !GetAtt WebServerInstance.AvailabilityZone
A deployment pattern where infrastructure is split into separate stacks by function (network, database, application), allowing teams to manage their own layers independently.
The AWS Console visual editor for CloudFormation templates (formerly called CloudFormation Designer). Displays templates as architecture diagrams with an integrated code editor.
A CloudFormation resource attribute that pauses stack creation until the resource sends a success signal via cfn-signal, ensuring the resource is fully initialized before the stack reports success.
A template that contains the software configuration (OS, application server, applications) required to launch an EC2 instance.
A service that stores configuration data and secrets. CloudFormation can reference SSM parameters in templates to dynamically resolve values like the latest AMI ID.
A script passed to an EC2 instance at launch time that runs automatically to configure the instance — used in this lab to install and start the Apache web server.
A virtual firewall for EC2 instances that controls inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level. Security groups are stateful — return traffic is automatically allowed.
A logically isolated section of the AWS cloud where you can launch AWS resources in a virtual network you define.
A VPC component that allows communication between instances in your VPC and the internet. Must be attached to a VPC and referenced in route tables for internet access.
YAML Ain't Markup Language — a human-readable data serialization format used for CloudFormation templates. Preferred over JSON for its cleaner syntax and easier readability.
CloudFormation's automatic recovery mechanism. If a stack update fails, CloudFormation rolls back all changes to restore the stack to its last known good state.
